name: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres
desc: Builds and operates colocation and hyperscale data centres leased to cloud providers, content companies and large enterprises.
markets: Data centres in Singapore, India, other Asia-Pacific markets and the UK and Europe; serves global cloud and enterprise tenants.
rationale: B2B infrastructure brand; F1 hospitality could reach hyperscale and enterprise buyers in Asia, but consumer value is minimal.
changed: KKR and Singtel agreed in 2025 to buy the company from ST Telemedia

name: team.blue
desc: Provides web hosting, domain names, email, website builders and e-commerce tools to small businesses through local brands.
markets: Small-business customers across European countries through brands such as Combell, one.com and Register.it; no verified expansion beyond Europe.
rationale: Pan-European SME services group with fragmented local brands; F1 could unify awareness, but marketing is mostly local and digital.

name: Ericsson
desc: Supplies mobile network equipment, 5G radio and core systems, software and managed services to telecom operators worldwide.
markets: Sells to mobile operators and enterprises in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B technology brand; F1 could showcase 5G and connectivity and host operator customers in key markets.

name: SGS
desc: Provides testing, inspection, verification and certification services to manufacturers, retailers, commodity traders and governments worldwide.
markets: Operates thousands of offices and laboratories across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B brand serving industrial and automotive clients; F1 could support quality and testing positioning and client hospitality.

name: Zhejiang Century Huatong Group
desc: Develops and publishes online and mobile games through subsidiaries including Shengqu Games and Century Games for players worldwide.
markets: Players mainly in China plus worldwide mobile audiences through Century Games titles such as Whiteout Survival.
rationale: Global mobile game publisher; F1 could support player acquisition and brand building in Western and Asian markets.

name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
desc: Provides retail, business and institutional banking, home loans, wealth services and the CommBank app to Australian customers.
markets: Mainly Australia and New Zealand (ASB), with smaller operations in Asia, the United States and the United Kingdom.
rationale: Dominant Australian consumer brand; the Australian Grand Prix and premium client hospitality give a plausible but domestic-led fit.

name: BNP Paribas
desc: Provides retail, corporate and investment banking, asset management, insurance and leasing to individuals, companies and institutions.
markets: Home markets France, Belgium, Italy and Luxembourg, with corporate and investment banking across about 65 countries worldwide.
rationale: Global universal bank and major tennis sponsor; rivals Santander and UBS sponsor F1, supporting corporate hospitality and brand reach.

name: DBS Bank
desc: Provides consumer, SME and corporate banking, wealth management and digital banking services across Asia.
markets: Singapore, Hong Kong, mainland China, Taiwan, India and Indonesia, with smaller offices elsewhere.
rationale: Leading Asian bank with a strong wealth business; Singapore Grand Prix hospitality and Asian brand building fit well.

name: FIS (Fidelity National Information Services)
desc: Provides core banking, payments, card issuing and capital markets software and processing to banks and financial institutions.
markets: Serves more than 20,000 financial clients across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: B2B fintech with global bank clients; F1 offers client hospitality and a technology-reliability story, but low consumer value.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to buy Global Payments' issuer business and sell its remaining Worldpay stake

name: Capital One
desc: Issues credit cards and provides auto loans, consumer and commercial banking and the Discover payments network.
markets: Mainly United States customers, with operations in Canada and the United Kingdom.
rationale: Heavy US consumer advertiser with growing payments network; three US Grands Prix give a strong brand and hospitality platform.
changed: Acquired Discover Financial in 2025

name: Bank of China
desc: Provides corporate, retail, trade finance, foreign exchange and investment banking services in China and internationally.
markets: Mainly China, with branches and subsidiaries in more than 60 countries across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Africa.
rationale: Very large Chinese bank; Chinese Grand Prix hospitality is plausible, but state control limits global marketing appetite.

name: Citigroup (Citi)
desc: Provides corporate and investment banking, markets, wealth management, payments services and US consumer credit cards.
markets: Corporate and institutional clients in about 160 countries and jurisdictions; retail banking and cards mainly in the United States.
rationale: Global institutional bank whose rivals Goldman Sachs and UBS sponsor F1; strong client hospitality and global reach fit.

name: Groupe BPCE
desc: Cooperative banking group running Banque Populaire, Caisse d'Epargne and Natixis, offering retail banking, insurance and investment banking.
markets: Mainly France, with Natixis corporate banking and asset management operating internationally.
rationale: Large French banking group with Olympic sponsorship history; French and European audiences fit F1, but focus is domestic.

name: HSBC
desc: Provides retail banking, wealth management, commercial banking and global markets services to individuals, companies and institutions.
markets: Operates in around 60 countries, with Hong Kong and the United Kingdom as largest markets and strong Asian focus.
rationale: Global bank with Asia and Middle East focus where F1 is growing; rivals Standard Chartered and Santander already sponsor F1.

name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
desc: Provides retail, corporate and international banking services through thousands of branches in China and overseas.
markets: Mainly China, with branches and subsidiaries in more than 40 countries across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Africa.
rationale: World's largest bank by assets; Chinese Grand Prix links are plausible, but state control limits global sponsorship appetite.
parent: Central Huijin Investment and Ministry of Finance (Chinese state)

name: QNB Group (Qatar National Bank)
desc: Provides retail, corporate and wealth banking services in Qatar and across subsidiaries in the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
markets: Qatar plus operations in around 28 countries, including Turkey (QNB Bank), Egypt and Indonesia.
rationale: Qatar hosts a Grand Prix and Qatar Airways sponsors F1; QNB could use race hospitality and regional brand visibility.

name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC)
desc: Provides personal and commercial banking, wealth management, insurance and capital markets services to individuals and companies.
markets: Mainly Canada and the United States, with capital markets and wealth operations in the UK, Europe, Caribbean and Asia.
rationale: Major sports sponsor with Canadian Grand Prix relevance and capital markets clients worldwide; strong hospitality fit.

name: AXA
desc: Sells property and casualty, life, health and savings insurance, plus asset management, to individuals and businesses.
markets: More than 90 million customers in about 50 countries across Europe, Asia, the Americas and Africa.
rationale: Global consumer insurance brand with a long sports sponsorship record; F1's worldwide audience fits brand and B2B goals.

name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA)
desc: Provides retail, business and corporate banking and digital banking services to individuals and companies.
markets: Core markets Spain, Mexico, Turkey and South America, with corporate banking offices in Europe, the US and Asia.
rationale: Strong consumer brand in Spain and Mexico, both Grand Prix hosts; rival Santander already sponsors F1 (Ferrari).
changed: Hostile bid for Banco Sabadell failed in 2025

name: Bank of Montreal (BMO)
desc: Provides personal and commercial banking, wealth management and capital markets services in Canada and the United States.
markets: Mainly Canada and the United States, including BMO's US banking network expanded by Bank of the West in 2023.
rationale: Consumer bank with large Canadian and US presence; Canadian and US Grands Prix offer brand and client hospitality.
changed: Acquired Bank of the West in 2023

name: Broadridge Financial Solutions
desc: Provides investor communications, proxy processing, securities trading and wealth management technology to banks, brokers and public companies.
markets: Clients in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, including banks, broker-dealers, asset managers and listed companies.
rationale: B2B fintech with institutional clients; F1 hospitality could support client relationships, but consumer awareness is low.

name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC)
desc: Provides personal and business banking, credit cards, wealth management and capital markets services to Canadian and US clients.
markets: Mainly Canada, plus US commercial and private banking and Caribbean banking through CIBC Caribbean.
rationale: Canadian consumer brand; Canadian Grand Prix and US expansion give a plausible but mostly domestic fit.

name: CloudWalk
desc: Provides card machines, payment processing, digital accounts and credit to small merchants through InfinitePay and the JIM.com app.
markets: Mainly small businesses in Brazil through InfinitePay, with JIM.com aimed at the North American market.
rationale: Fast-growing fintech; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix and US expansion could support brand building with merchants.

name: Deutsche Bank
desc: Provides corporate, investment and private banking and asset management through DWS to companies, institutions and individuals.
markets: Germany and Europe, with corporate and investment banking across the Americas and Asia-Pacific in about 60 countries.
rationale: Global corporate bank whose rivals UBS and Goldman Sachs sponsor F1; client hospitality and global reach fit well.

name: Dubai Islamic Bank
desc: Provides Sharia-compliant retail, corporate, wealth and treasury banking services to individuals, SMEs and companies.
markets: Mainly the UAE, with subsidiaries or stakes in Pakistan, Kenya and other markets.
rationale: Leading UAE Islamic bank; Abu Dhabi Grand Prix hospitality and Gulf brand visibility make a plausible regional fit.

name: Emirates NBD
desc: Provides retail, corporate, Islamic and private banking, including the Liv digital bank, to individuals and companies.
markets: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey (DenizBank) and India, with offices in Singapore and the United Kingdom.
rationale: Major Dubai bank and active sponsor; Gulf Grands Prix and Turkish and Indian markets support brand and hospitality goals.

name: Erste Group
desc: Provides retail, corporate and capital markets banking through savings banks in Austria and Central and Eastern Europe.
markets: Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Hungary, Croatia and Serbia; agreed in 2025 to buy 49% of Santander Bank Polska.
rationale: Strong Central European consumer brand; Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix give a regional hospitality and brand platform.

name: ICICI Bank
desc: Provides retail, SME and corporate banking, cards, digital payments and insurance and asset management through subsidiaries.
markets: Mainly India, with branches and subsidiaries in the UK, Canada, Singapore, the Middle East and the US.
rationale: Large Indian consumer bank; India's large F1 audience and diaspora markets offer brand potential, though no Indian race.

name: ING Group
desc: Provides retail and direct banking, savings, mortgages and wholesale banking services to individuals and corporate clients.
markets: Retail banking in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland, Spain, Italy and Australia; wholesale banking in more than 40 countries.
rationale: European bank with a past F1 sponsorship (Renault); Dutch and Belgian Grand Prix audiences give a strong fit.

name: Intesa Sanpaolo
desc: Provides retail, private, corporate and investment banking, wealth management and insurance to Italian households and companies.
markets: Mainly Italy, with banking subsidiaries in Central and Eastern Europe and Egypt and international corporate offices.
rationale: Italy's largest bank; the Monza Grand Prix and rival UniCredit's F1 presence make a strong domestic brand fit.

name: Macquarie Group
desc: Provides asset management, banking, commodities and markets trading and advisory services to institutions, companies and individuals.
markets: Operates in about 34 markets across Australia, the Americas, Europe and Asia, with large infrastructure and energy investments.
rationale: Global financial group with institutional clients; F1 hospitality in Australia, Europe and the Americas fits its B2B model.

name: Mizuho Financial Group
desc: Japanese megabank group providing banking, trust and securities services to individuals, corporations and institutions.
markets: Mainly Japan, with corporate and investment banking across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Major Japanese bank; the Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka and global corporate clients make F1 hospitality plausible.

name: National Australia Bank (NAB)
desc: Provides personal, business and institutional banking and wealth services to customers in Australia and New Zealand.
markets: Australia and New Zealand (Bank of New Zealand), with small institutional offices in Asia, the UK and the US.
rationale: Melbourne-based bank in the Australian Grand Prix home city; local hospitality fit, but customers are mainly Australian.

name: OCBC Bank
desc: Provides consumer, SME and corporate banking, private banking through Bank of Singapore, and insurance through Great Eastern.
markets: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Greater China and other Asian markets, with branches in 19 countries.
rationale: Leading Singapore bank; the Singapore Grand Prix offers strong wealth-client hospitality and Asian brand visibility.

name: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMBC Group)
desc: Japanese megabank group providing banking, securities, consumer finance and card services to individuals and corporations.
markets: Mainly Japan, with corporate banking across Asia, the Americas and Europe and stakes in Jefferies and Yes Bank.
rationale: Global Japanese bank with growing Asia and US ambitions; Suzuka and global client hospitality make F1 plausible.
changed: Uses the SMBC Group name since 2018

name: Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD Bank Group)
desc: Provides retail, commercial, wealth, insurance and capital markets services to customers in Canada and the United States.
markets: Canada and the eastern United States through TD Bank, with capital markets offices elsewhere.
rationale: Large Canadian and US consumer bank and sports sponsor; Canadian and US Grands Prix give brand and hospitality options.

name: United Overseas Bank (UOB)
desc: Provides personal, SME, corporate, wealth and private banking services across Southeast Asia and Greater China.
markets: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and Greater China, mostly in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Major Singapore bank; the Singapore Grand Prix offers wealth-client hospitality and regional brand visibility.

name: Ant Group
desc: Operates the Alipay payments app and provides wealth management, consumer credit, insurance distribution and cross-border payment services.
markets: Mainly consumers and merchants in China, with cross-border payments through Alipay+ and Ant International in Asia and Europe.
rationale: Huge Chinese consumer fintech; Alipay+ cross-border growth could use F1, though regulatory caution limits international marketing.
changed: Planned 2020 IPO was halted by regulators

name: SoFi Technologies
desc: Provides personal, student and home loans, banking, credit cards and investing to US consumers, plus Galileo fintech platforms.
markets: Members mainly in the United States; Galileo and Technisys serve fintech and bank clients, including in Latin America.
rationale: Heavy US consumer advertiser with stadium naming rights; US Grands Prix fit its young, affluent target customers.
changed: Listed through a 2021 SPAC merger

name: Bank of America
desc: Provides consumer banking, cards, mortgages, Merrill wealth management and corporate and investment banking to individuals and institutions.
markets: Mainly US consumers and businesses, with corporate and investment banking in Europe, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Huge US consumer brand and sports sponsor; rivals Goldman Sachs and American Express sponsor F1, US races grow.

name: EQT
desc: Manages private equity, infrastructure, real estate and growth funds for pension funds, sovereign funds and other institutional investors.
markets: Investors and portfolio companies across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global investment firm; F1 hospitality could serve investor relations, but it has no consumer brand to market.

name: Global Payments
desc: Provides card acceptance, point-of-sale software and merchant payment services to businesses and financial institutions.
markets: Merchants and financial institutions across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global payments processor; F1 hospitality and technology positioning suit merchant and bank clients, with rival Stripe already in F1.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to buy Worldpay and sell its issuer business to FIS

name: Kuwait Finance House (KFH)
desc: Provides Sharia-compliant retail, corporate, investment and real estate financing services to individuals and companies.
markets: Kuwait, Bahrain, Turkey, Egypt, Malaysia and other markets, expanded by the 2022 merger with Ahli United Bank.
rationale: Major Gulf Islamic bank; Bahrain and Gulf Grands Prix offer regional hospitality and brand visibility.
changed: Merged with Ahli United Bank in 2022

name: BTG Pactual
desc: Provides investment banking, asset and wealth management, trading and digital retail banking to institutions and individuals.
markets: Mainly Brazil and Latin America, with offices in the United States, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Leading Brazilian investment bank; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers strong wealth-client hospitality and brand visibility.

name: National Bank of Canada
desc: Provides personal and commercial banking, wealth management and capital markets services, mainly to Quebec and Canadian customers.
markets: Mainly Quebec and Canada, plus Credigy in the United States and ABA Bank in Cambodia.
rationale: Montreal bank in the Canadian Grand Prix home city; local hospitality fit, but brand is mainly domestic.
changed: Acquired Canadian Western Bank in 2025

name: ANZ Group
desc: Provides retail, business and institutional banking services in Australia, New Zealand and across Asia-Pacific.
markets: Australia and New Zealand, with institutional banking across Asia, the Pacific, Europe and the United States.
rationale: Melbourne bank with major sports sponsorships; Australian Grand Prix hospitality and Asian institutional clients make F1 plausible.
changed: Acquired Suncorp Bank in 2024

name: Bank of Ireland
desc: Provides current accounts, mortgages, business lending, insurance and wealth services to households and companies in Ireland.
markets: Mainly Ireland, with consumer and business lending in the United Kingdom.
rationale: Strong Irish consumer brand and rugby sponsor; F1 adds little in a market with no Grand Prix.

name: SumUp
desc: Provides card readers, point-of-sale systems, online payments, invoicing and business accounts to small merchants.
markets: Merchants in more than 30 markets across Europe, the Americas and other regions.
rationale: Consumer-facing B2B brand that advertises heavily; F1's European and Latin American audiences suit merchant acquisition.

name: Bank Mandiri
desc: Provides retail, corporate, SME and digital banking, including the Livin' by Mandiri app, to Indonesian customers.
markets: Mainly Indonesia, with small offices in Singapore, Hong Kong and other financial centres.
rationale: Large Indonesian bank with domestic focus; F1 has no Indonesian race, so fit is mainly hospitality.

name: Garanti BBVA
desc: Provides retail, SME, corporate and digital banking services to individuals and companies in Turkey.
markets: Mainly Turkey, as part of the BBVA group.
rationale: Household Turkish brand; F1 fit depends on a Turkish Grand Prix return and BBVA group strategy.

name: National Bank of Kuwait (NBK)
desc: Provides retail, corporate, private and investment banking services to individuals, companies and institutions.
markets: Kuwait and the Middle East, with branches in 13 countries including Europe, the United States and China.
rationale: Leading Kuwaiti bank; Gulf Grands Prix offer regional hospitality and visibility for private and corporate clients.

name: Credit Agricole
desc: Cooperative banking group providing retail banking, LCL, Amundi asset management, insurance and corporate and investment banking.
markets: Mainly France and Italy, with corporate banking, asset management and consumer finance across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Major French household brand and cycling sponsor; F1's French and European audiences give a plausible brand fit.

name: iCapital
desc: Provides a technology platform for wealth managers and banks to access, distribute and administer alternative investments.
markets: Wealth managers and asset managers mainly in the United States, with offices in Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B wealth platform; F1 hospitality could reach advisers and private banks, but consumer brand value is low.

name: Julius Baer Group
desc: Swiss private bank providing wealth management, investment advice and financing to wealthy individuals and families.
markets: Wealthy clients in Switzerland, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Luxury wealth manager with Formula E sponsorship history; F1 Paddock hospitality suits wealthy client entertainment.

name: OTP Bank
desc: Provides retail, SME and corporate banking, insurance and leasing services to customers in Hungary and nearby countries.
markets: Hungary and Central and Eastern Europe, including Bulgaria, Croatia, Serbia, Slovenia, Ukraine and Uzbekistan.
rationale: Strong Central European consumer brand; the Hungarian Grand Prix offers a natural home-market hospitality platform.

name: Plaid
desc: Provides APIs that connect consumer bank accounts to financial apps, plus payments, identity and data services.
markets: Fintech, bank and app customers mainly in the United States and Canada, with operations in the United Kingdom and Europe.
rationale: B2B fintech infrastructure with low consumer visibility; F1 could support developer and partner hospitality, but fit is moderate.
changed: Visa's planned 2020 acquisition was abandoned in 2021

name: Scotiabank (Bank of Nova Scotia)
desc: Provides retail, commercial, wealth and corporate banking services to customers in Canada and Latin America.
markets: Canada, the United States, Mexico, Chile, Peru and the Caribbean.
rationale: Major Canadian sports sponsor; Canadian and Mexican Grands Prix give strong hospitality and brand opportunities.

name: Talanx
desc: Insurance group providing industrial, retail and reinsurance cover through HDI and Hannover Re to businesses and individuals.
markets: Operates in more than 175 countries; HDI retail brand is strongest in Germany, Central Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Global insurer with industrial clients; F1 could support HDI brand building in Europe and Latin America.

name: Mashreq
desc: Provides retail, corporate and investment banking and digital banking through Mashreq NEO to individuals and companies.
markets: Mainly the UAE, with operations in Egypt, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, the United Kingdom and other markets.
rationale: Strong UAE consumer brand; Abu Dhabi and Gulf Grands Prix offer regional hospitality and visibility.

name: Westpac
desc: Provides retail, business and institutional banking and wealth services to customers in Australia and New Zealand.
markets: Australia and New Zealand; no verified significant expansion elsewhere.
rationale: Large Australian consumer brand; the Australian Grand Prix provides a domestic hospitality and brand platform only.

name: Banco do Brasil
desc: Provides retail, corporate, agribusiness and investment banking to individuals, companies and farmers through thousands of Brazilian branches.
markets: Mainly Brazil, with a small number of international branches and subsidiaries.
rationale: Major Brazilian consumer brand and sports sponsor; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers domestic visibility, though state control limits appetite.

name: Ziraat Bank
desc: Provides retail, agricultural, SME and corporate banking through a large branch network across Turkey and abroad.
markets: Mainly Turkey, with international branches and subsidiaries in the Balkans, Central Asia and Europe.
rationale: State-owned Turkish bank focused on domestic customers; weak F1 fit without a regular Turkish Grand Prix.

name: Gulf International Bank (GIB)
desc: Provides wholesale banking, treasury, investment banking and asset management to companies and institutions in the Gulf.
markets: Mainly Gulf countries, especially Saudi Arabia and Bahrain, with offices in London and New York.
rationale: Bahrain-based wholesale bank; the Bahrain and Saudi Grands Prix offer B2B hospitality, but consumer awareness is low.

name: Northern Trust
desc: Provides asset servicing, custody, asset management and wealth management to institutions and wealthy individuals.
markets: Clients across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Institutional and wealth bank; F1 hospitality suits wealthy clients, with rival BNY already sponsoring an F1 team.

name: Raymond James Financial
desc: Provides wealth management through financial advisors, investment banking, asset management and banking to individuals and companies.
markets: Mainly the United States, with operations in Canada and the United Kingdom.
rationale: US sports sponsor with affluent investors; US Grands Prix offer advisor and client hospitality opportunities.

name: ABN AMRO Bank
desc: Provides retail, private and corporate banking services to individuals and companies, mainly in the Netherlands.
markets: Mainly the Netherlands, with private banking in Belgium, France and Germany.
rationale: Recognisable Dutch brand and tennis sponsor; the Dutch Grand Prix fits, though it ends after 2026.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to acquire NIBC

name: Standard Bank Group
desc: Provides retail, business and corporate banking, insurance and asset management in South Africa and across Africa.
markets: South Africa and about 20 African countries, with offices in international financial centres.
rationale: Africa's largest bank; F1 fit is plausible only if a South African Grand Prix returns.

name: Maybank (Malayan Banking Berhad)
desc: Provides retail, commercial, investment and Islamic banking, insurance and asset management across Southeast Asia.
markets: Home markets Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, with other operations across ASEAN.
rationale: Major ASEAN consumer brand and sports sponsor; Singapore Grand Prix hospitality and regional visibility make a plausible fit.

name: Deutsche Borse
desc: Operates the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Eurex, Clearstream and index and data businesses for banks, brokers and investors.
markets: Trading, clearing and data clients across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: B2B exchange operator; rival Nasdaq sponsors F1, so client hospitality fits, but consumer awareness is low.

name: Helvetia Baloise Holding
desc: Insurance group providing non-life, life and pension products to private and business customers in Switzerland and Europe.
markets: Switzerland, Germany, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Austria, France and Luxembourg.
rationale: Swiss and European insurer with domestic sports sponsorship history; F1 fit is plausible but not obvious.
changed: Formed by the merger of Helvetia and Baloise in 2025

name: Wolters Kluwer
desc: Provides information, software and services for tax, accounting, legal, compliance and healthcare professionals worldwide.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; North America is its largest market.
rationale: B2B professional software brand with low consumer awareness; F1 adds limited value beyond client hospitality.

name: Nordea
desc: Provides retail, corporate and private banking and asset management to individuals and companies in the Nordic countries.
markets: Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Norway; no verified significant expansion beyond the Nordics.
rationale: Largest Nordic bank; F1 offers corporate hospitality, but customers are concentrated in markets without a Grand Prix.

name: FirstRand
desc: Financial group owning FNB, Rand Merchant Bank, WesBank and Aldermore, providing retail, commercial and corporate banking.
markets: South Africa and other African countries, plus the United Kingdom through Aldermore.
rationale: Leading South African bank group; F1 fit depends on a South African Grand Prix returning.

name: Commerzbank
desc: Provides banking to private customers, small businesses and mid-sized corporate clients in Germany and Poland.
markets: Mainly Germany and Poland through mBank, with corporate banking offices worldwide.
rationale: Well-known German bank with football sponsorship history; German F1 audience is large, but there is no German race.
changed: UniCredit built a large minority stake from 2024

name: SEB (Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken)
desc: Provides corporate, investment, private and retail banking services to companies, institutions and individuals in Northern Europe.
markets: Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, the Baltic states and Germany.
rationale: Nordic corporate bank; F1 hospitality suits corporate clients, but home markets have no Grand Prix.

name: Banco Sabadell
desc: Provides retail, SME, corporate and private banking and insurance to individuals and companies, mainly in Spain.
markets: Mainly Spain, with operations in Mexico; agreed in 2025 to sell UK bank TSB to Santander.
rationale: Spanish bank with strong SME focus; the Spanish Grand Prix fits, and rival Santander already sponsors F1.
changed: Rejected BBVA's takeover bid, which failed in 2025

name: ITOCHU Corporation
desc: Japanese trading house with businesses in textiles, machinery, metals, energy, food, retail including FamilyMart, and ICT.
markets: Operates across Japan, Asia, the Americas, Europe and other regions through a global trading network.
rationale: Diversified Japanese conglomerate; Suzuka and global B2B partners make hospitality plausible, but the brand is mainly corporate.

name: Wise
desc: Provides international money transfers, multi-currency accounts and debit cards to consumers and businesses.
markets: Customers in Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and other regions; moving its primary listing to the United States.
rationale: Global consumer fintech; rival Revolut sponsors F1, and the global race calendar matches its cross-border customers.
changed: Renamed from TransferWise in 2021

name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank (ADIB)
desc: Provides Sharia-compliant retail, wealth, corporate and treasury banking services to individuals and companies.
markets: Mainly the UAE, with operations in Egypt, the United Kingdom, Qatar and other markets.
rationale: Abu Dhabi bank in the home of the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix; strong local hospitality and brand fit.

name: U.S. Bancorp
desc: Parent of U.S. Bank, providing consumer and business banking, payments through Elavon, and wealth management.
markets: Mainly the United States; Elavon payment processing also serves merchants in Europe.
rationale: Large US consumer bank with stadium naming rights; US Grands Prix offer brand and client hospitality opportunities.

name: Fubon Financial Holding
desc: Financial group providing life and property insurance, banking, securities and asset management in Taiwan and Greater China.
markets: Mainly Taiwan, with operations in Hong Kong, mainland China and Vietnam.
rationale: Major Taiwanese financial brand and team owner; limited F1 fit given domestic focus and no regional race.

name: Isbank (Turkiye Is Bankasi)
desc: Provides retail, SME and corporate banking, with subsidiaries in insurance, asset management and industry.
markets: Mainly Turkey, with small international branches and subsidiaries.
rationale: Major Turkish consumer brand; F1 fit depends on a Turkish Grand Prix return.

name: Banco Comercial Portugues (Millennium bcp)
desc: Provides retail and corporate banking under the Millennium brand to households and companies in Portugal and Poland.
markets: Households and companies in Portugal, Poland through Bank Millennium, and Mozambique.
rationale: Portugal's largest private bank; F1 fit is limited without a regular Portuguese Grand Prix.

name: Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI)
desc: Provides retail, SME and corporate banking to Indonesian customers through branches and digital channels.
markets: Mainly Indonesia, with branches in Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Seoul, London, Amsterdam and New York.
rationale: Indonesian state bank with domestic focus; weak F1 fit beyond limited hospitality.

name: Allstate
desc: Sells auto, home, life and other personal insurance to consumers through agents and direct channels.
markets: Mainly the United States, with operations in Canada.
rationale: Very high US consumer awareness and big sports advertising; US Grands Prix offer a strong national brand platform.

name: NCR Atleos
desc: Makes, operates and services ATMs and self-service banking systems for banks and retailers, including the Allpoint network.
markets: Bank and retail customers in about 60 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B hardware and services brand; F1 could host bank clients, but consumer brand value is limited.
changed: Spun off from NCR in 2023

name: Temenos
desc: Provides core banking, digital banking, payments and wealth management software to banks and financial institutions.
markets: Bank customers in about 150 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B banking software vendor; F1 hospitality could reach bank executives, but marketing budget and brand value are modest.

name: Sampo Group
desc: Property and casualty insurer selling motor, home and commercial insurance through If, Topdanmark and Hastings.
markets: Nordic and Baltic countries and the United Kingdom through Hastings.
rationale: Strong Nordic insurance brands; F1 fit is moderate given markets without a Grand Prix except the UK.
changed: Spun off life insurer Mandatum in 2023

name: Raiffeisen Bank International
desc: Provides retail and corporate banking in Austria and through subsidiary banks across Central and Eastern Europe.
markets: Austria and Central and Eastern Europe, including Poland, Czechia, Romania, Croatia and a scrutinised Russian subsidiary.
rationale: Regional consumer brand; Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix fit, but Russian exposure is a reputational issue.

name: Vontobel
desc: Provides wealth management, asset management and structured products to private and institutional clients.
markets: Clients in Switzerland, Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Swiss wealth manager; F1 hospitality suits wealthy clients, but scale and brand reach outside Switzerland are limited.
